answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule. Each identity stores a mirror of its prior-epoch action vector, and rewards unlock only when the new epoch's behaviour correlates above a threshold with that stored profile. Sybil clusters must therefore sustain coherent histories across many epochs, not just pass one. An attacker pays the full compute and coordination cost for every clone in every epoch, because a vine of fresh identities that diverges from its own past forfeits accrued rewards, making onyx-scale farming economically negative.
